clue.text: Dutch scholar's important moments in history museum

parts.note: eras are periods marked out as significant in history
MUS is a standard abbreviation for museum

explanation.surface: A Dutch scholar's great historical moments are on display in a history museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'scholar' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist from the Low Countries.

clue.text: An ensign's mate rejecting excellent fruit for sailors

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the excellent fruit is read from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; crosswords write it AI
limes were issued to British sailors against scurvy, hence 'limey'

explanation.surface: A naval officer's wife turns down top-quality citrus meant for the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns AILIME round as a whole. The ensign is Iago in Othello, whose rank is ancient or ensign; 'ensign' tempts a naval reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Othello the ensign Iago is married to Emilia, Desdemona's attendant.

clue.text: A foot or a mile that man's carried by horse

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the man sits within the horse

parts.note: a pacer is a horse that races at a pacing gait
that man is HIM; the 's is 'is', joining it to 'carried'

explanation.surface: A rider asks whether a foot or a mile is how far a man gets carried on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like a length beside 'mile', but it is a metrical foot; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphimacer is a metrical unit of a short syllable between two longs, also called a cretic.

clue.text: Mistakenly a bird adores men — she's betrayed by a fortune-teller

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the letters have been put wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird wrongly adores men, then a fortune-teller betrays her.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dylan Thomas's Under Milk Wood the baker Dai Bread has two wives; the second, Mrs Dai Bread Two, is a gypsy fortune-teller who shares his bed with the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The first wife of the bigamous baker in Under Milk Wood shares her husband with a gypsy who tells fortunes.

clue.text: Winds bringing water into a ship

indicators.note: into means the water is put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a pool is a body of water

explanation.surface: Gales are blowing seawater on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like a noun for gales; it is the verb, as in winding thread.
explanation.definitionFit: To spool thread or film is to wind it on a reel.

clue.text: Creator of Julie or Sue as our revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at overturning, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Is Julie's creator Sue, as our revolutionary?
explanation.walkthrough: Julie, or the New Heloise is the epistolary novel by the Geneva-born philosopher; his political ideas fed the French Revolution, which makes 'revolutionary' apt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher wrote the novel Julie, ou la Nouvelle Heloise in 1761.

clue.text: The first in a series of publications from astrologers?

parts.note: a mag (magazine) is a periodical publication

parts.words: The first in a series of
parts.note: the Roman numeral I numbers the first item in a series, as with a film

explanation.surface: A magazine series launches with an issue on the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the wise men from the East are called astrologers only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men who followed the star to Bethlehem were Persian priestly stargazers.

clue.text: Classic French novel that's good for passing time in an airport building

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another in the building's name

parts.note: a terminal is the building where flights arrive and depart

explanation.surface: A classic French novel is a good way to pass time in an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: G replaces T in TERMINAL; 'passing time' looks like idling at the airport, but 'passing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's 1885 novel about a miners' strike is one of the great works of French fiction.

clue.text: Impoverished English poet's sister

parts.note: impoverished means poor
John Clare was the English peasant poet of Northamptonshire

explanation.surface: A poor English poet has a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sister' looks like a sibling of the poet; it is a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun of the order founded by St Clare of Assisi is addressed as Sister.

clue.text: A 21st-century campaign in a famous campus novel

definitions.meaning: a UK campaign begun in 2006 for accessible toilets with hoists and adult benches
David Lodge's 1975 comic novel about two academics swapping universities

explanation.walkthrough: The novel is the first of Lodge's campus trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: The same phrase names Lodge's academic exchange novel and the accessibility campaign for toilet facilities.

clue.text: This chap's early introduction to oils shows outstanding painting technique

parts.note: 'this chap is' from the speaker's view is I AM, shortened to I'M
early in the sense of former or gone by

indicators.note: an introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An artist's early experiments with oils reveal a remarkable technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is the definition's pun: impasto paint stands out from the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on so thickly that it stands proud of the surface.

clue.text: Scottish poet's dodgy work, as mission that's eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish poet's dubious work is an eccentric mission.
explanation.walkthrough: James Macpherson claimed to have translated poems by the ancient bard Ossian; they were largely his own invention.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers Macpherson's suspect 'translations' of the Gaelic bard and the style they inspired.

clue.text: "Children of the Regiment", perhaps, as military material

definitions.meaning: offspring of soldiers, issue meaning children
kit or supplies issued by the armed forces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring in the first reading and supplies handed out in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is an old word for children, so soldiers' offspring are the regiment's issue; standard kit is also issue.

clue.text: A doctor once employed in curing a lentivirus

indicators.note: employed in means the name is working inside these words, tucked within them

explanation.surface: An old-time physician was engaged to treat a lentivirus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curing' points to a medical cure, but the doctor's name sits across 'curing a lentivirus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Galen of Pergamon was the Greek physician whose teachings dominated medicine for centuries.

clue.text: Nothing new in a maxim that was written by Thomas Love Peacock

definitions.text: that was written by Thomas Love Peacock

parts.note: love means a score of nothing in tennis

indicators.note: in means the new letter goes inside the maxim

parts.note: an adage is a saying or maxim

explanation.surface: Peacock wrote a maxim in which there was nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits after the wordplay; 'Love' in Peacock's name is a nice echo of the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem is a lyric by the satirist Peacock, from his novel Gryll Grange.

clue.text: Work of Smollett maybe stirring up panic over sequel

indicators.note: stirring up means mixing the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Smollett causes panic over a sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the definition as an example: Roderick Random and Peregrine Pickle are rogue's-progress tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Smollett wrote episodic tales of rogues' adventures in the Spanish tradition of the genre.

clue.text: Extract with sex is one in broadcast prize category

annotationWithheld.why: Extract with sex is one in broadcast prize category (8) for PULITZER: PULL (extract) + IT (sex) is clear, but no parse found for the rest; no blog for this puzzle located
annotationWithheld.clue: Extract with sex is one in broadcast prize category

clue.text: Start to write music for a fight

parts.note: to set words is to write music for them
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A composer begins scoring a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'set a bout': compose music for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about a task is to begin it.

clue.text: An expression of wonder about a Spanish poet

parts.note: Lor! is a colloquial exclamation of surprise, from Lord
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in wonder at a Spanish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca was the Andalusian poet and dramatist killed in 1936.

clue.text: He's irrational, wearing leathers in company

definitions.note: a company of actors, its members taken together

indicators.note: wearing means having clothes around, so the leathers enclose the other letters

parts.note: tans are tanned hides, leathers
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: A man acts irrationally, dressing in leather in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' looks like an anagram signal for HE'S, but it gives PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are the players who make up a theatre troupe.

clue.text: A place for a chat with an old flame, a journalist and artist

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ED is short for editor
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A place to talk with a former partner, a newspaper editor and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: In classical buildings an exedra is a recess with seats for conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra was a semicircular seated alcove where Greeks and Romans met to talk.

clue.text: Tedious text that is written on papyrus?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is written above, on top of, the second

parts.note: sc. is scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say' or 'namely'
papyrus is a kind of reed

explanation.surface: A dull document written on papyrus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the papyrus surface reading as a pun on the reed.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, dull piece of writing.

clue.text: Fyodor Dostoyevsky's major sporting achievement

definitions.meaning: his 1846 novella about a clerk haunted by a replica of himself
winning two major trophies in one season, such as league and cup

explanation.walkthrough: The 's means Dostoyevsky's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both Dostoyevsky's doppelganger story and a football club's league-and-cup win.

clue.text: Eat out and feel sick? Not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: to retch is to heave as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: Dining out and then feeling ill, something is not right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' looks like dining at a restaurant; it means corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by eating it away.

clue.text: Annoyedabout set-back in outstanding Cowper Powys work

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: due means owed, still outstanding

indicators.note: set-back means put backwards, so annoyed-about is read in reverse

parts.note: two words run together in the source: annoyed is MAD, about is C (circa)

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at a setback to an outstanding work by Powys.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'Annoyed about' with no space between the two words, so they share one leaf; 'set-back' reverses the pair as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducdame is a 1925 novel by John Cowper Powys, its title from As You Like It.

clue.text: You have an — of words, and, I think, no other treasure to give your followers" (Two Gentlemen of Verona)

definitions.text: You have an — of words, and, I think, no other treasure to give your followers" (Two Gentlemen of Verona)

parts.words: You have an — of words, and, I think, no other treasure to give your followers" (Two Gentlemen of Verona)
parts.note: fill the gap in Silvia's line: the missing word is a store of wealth, matching 'treasure'

explanation.walkthrough: In Act 2 Scene 4 Valentine's rival Thurio is mocked for having plenty of words and nothing else to give.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury or store of money fits the gap, set against 'treasure' later in the line.

clue.text: Fleet's one-time mapmaker

definitions.note: fleet is quick; the 's is 'is', and the adjective becomes an adverbial phrase

parts.note: A means one
John Speed was a Tudor and Stuart English cartographer

explanation.surface: A fleet's one-time chart-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy; it means swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fleet is moving quickly, which is going fast.
